result.summary: WF-03 Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER) produced the Type E prose fix design for the residual-29 T010 hardcoded-UUID migration at src/design/iss0121_residual29_migration.md. The design re-uses the existing TestHarness.newUuid (helpers.zig:467) and TestHarness.newUuidString (helpers.zig:479) API verbatim — no new helper, no wrapper, no new module. The 29 affected files split into four BACKEND-DEV-friendly batches (8/8/8/5 files; 27/79/53/9 active T010 literals) with explicit per-batch file sets and per-file per-call replacement strategies (Pattern P1 instance-id → newUuidString + defer; P2 actor-id typed [16]u8 → newUuid direct; P3 audit-id → binding passed into both INSERT and SELECT; P4 module-const forbidden outcome). Four per-batch validation gates defined (G1 lint strictly decreases with exact delta computed from live `--json` output; G2 zig build test exits 0; G3 focused integration test; G4 full integration suite green). Stale-inventory handling rule explicitly forbids refreshing tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json to mask new violations. T010 → BLOCKER promotion at tools/lint_test_isolation.py:84 is the deferred goal of the run and is gated on the post-Batch-D live lint reporting MAJOR < 10; promotion MUST NOT happen earlier (would block the build with 168 active findings, which is a regression). T020 (3 findings) and T050 (3 findings) explicitly listed as out-of-scope (separate backlog entries recommended) — they are separately actionable lint defects requiring architectural changes beyond UUID isolation. Design contains no implementation code (no Zig function bodies, no SQL DDL, no linter regex rewrites, no baseline JSON diffs). INNER-REPORT registered at docs/issue-reports/WF03-gh402-20260803-step-02-code-designer-INNER-REPORT.yaml with constraints-satisfied cross-check against step-005's constraints list. Live lint at design time: BLOCKER=0 MAJOR=174 MINOR=0 across 122 files; 195 suppressed from baseline. Routing to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 2b — hard gate).

issues.description: On-disk residual figure (29 files, 174 MAJOR = 168 T010 + 3 T020 + 3 T050) is larger than the 24-file figure cited in the GH #402 body. The body was drafted against an earlier 17→24 mental model. The design §1 documents this explicitly; the §10 risks table names 'inventory drift' as a named risk so BACKEND-DEV trusts the live lint, not the prose counts. No change to GH #402 required; the issue title already says 'residual-29'.

Three T020 (module-level mutable var) and three T050 (no BPM_TEST_DB_URL reference) findings exist in the residual-29 file set but are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this migration. They are separately actionable lint defects (module-state hygiene and DB-env reference) and require architectural changes beyond UUID isolation. The design §6 'Out-of-scope findings' table lists them by file; BACKEND-DEV MUST NOT touch T020 or T050 during this migration.

tools/lint_test_isolation.py:84 is the single-line promotion point for the deferred MAJOR → BLOCKER change. The line number is correct as of the lint capture at 6cc92ec; if a future PR touches that file before this run's Batch D lands, the promotion point must be re-located. The design §9 step 4 flags this implicitly and §12 verification recipe step 'Gate G1-bis' confirms the promotion took effect.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-03 Step 2b — hard gate). The validator must apply the WF-03 Step 2b checklist (per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md): (a) design addresses the diagnosed root_cause from ISS-0121.json#root_cause (hardcoded fixture identity → per-test UUID generation), (b) public function signatures before/after are documented (Type E: the newUuid/newUuidString signatures are cited unchanged from helpers.zig:467/479), (c) no implementation code is present in the design, (d) error taxonomy is updated if error variants change (none changed; newUuidString still propagates only error.OutOfMemory), (e) callers that must be updated are listed (§5 batch file sets), (f) fix scope ≤ 5 files (the design exceeds 5 files but this is a documented cross-cutting migration of 29 files — the workflow rule allows ORCH escalation to architectural review; the design pre-emptively documents the > 5-file scope in §1 and §5). Implementation MUST NOT begin before the validator returns PASS. After validator PASS, ORCH routes to BACKEND-DEV (WF-03 Step 3) which applies the design mechanically per §5 (batches) and §6 (per-file patterns), running §7 validation gates after each batch.
